l.i: ORnatura diu non mittunt Pharmacopola Sarracene tuum munera connubium. Nam dicto citius rapidis gula dentibus illa Luxus & immitis cuncta vorare solet. Sed forsan qua dona tibi nunc parvula mitto Sunt mansura olim, sunt placitura simul. Exornent mensas bellaria lauta secundas, Illustrat sacras clara Camoena faces.

main_text.l: IOANNI IONSTONO SCOTO AD SACRVM VERBI Dei ministerium exercendum in patriam reuertenti 9. Mart. 1591.

l.i: ERgo Caledonia fines Ionstone reuisis, Et dulcis arua patriæ? Ergo paras tandem cœlesti nectare sacrum Ovile Christi pascere: Cœtibus atque piis fœcundo pectore iura Legis supremæ promere?

page.notes: The initial letters O and E are large woodcut initials. The ornamental band between the poems is a printer's woodcut, not text. The show-through from the reverse page is ignored. The final word is printed in italic at the lower right, rendered here as it appears on the scan; it is uncertain (marked by the apparent letters "Maɛte").
